body.estimand_functional: \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\theta\in\Theta:\text{the bias-aware transformed-outcome test at the scan-selected cutoff accepts }\theta\}\)

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and a law-specific unknown cutoff \(c_P\in[1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument is \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge c_P\}\), and monotone response types imply \(D_i=D_i(Z_i)\).
sampling_model.outcome: Binary potential outcomes obey consistency \(Y_i=Y_i(D_i)\); exclusion is encoded by the absence of a direct \(Z_i\) argument.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniformly on both sides of the cutoff, \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x,\ell)\ge v\) and the absolute conditional outcome--treatment correlation is at most \(1-v\); when the conditional treatment variance is zero, covariance is zero and the correlation inequality is interpreted directly without forming a correlation coefficient.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: One-sided observable treatment and outcome regressions admit radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions.  The proved \(s=1\) procedure uses deterministic four-fold splitting, fixed-denominator boundary-kernel treatment contrasts, a coarse \(H/64\)-resolution scan, an independent local mesh refinement, and fixed-center transformed-outcome inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 states that the bias-aware Anderson--Rubin confidence set is honest over the maintained known-cutoff class.
Their Theorem 4 establishes \(n\)-consistent cutoff estimation with a compound-Poisson argmax limit under a fixed discontinuity.
Their ordered-modulus construction minimizes expected length at a point subject to uniform coverage over a convex regression class.
Their Proposition 4.2 gives a matched minimax cutoff-location rate when the derivative jump is bounded away from zero.
Their multiscale estimator provides simultaneous change-point inference and exponential underestimation control for step functions.
Their Bayesian model propagates posterior uncertainty about an unknown cutoff into fuzzy-RD effect estimation.
Their working paper treats fuzzy regression discontinuity and unknown discontinuity estimation in separate high-dimensional extensions.

body.tldr: The paper studies fixed-\(\alpha\) expected length of connected honest intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE when both the compliance jump and its unknown cutoff become statistically weak.  The location-mixture constructions give a nonshrinking lower bound below the signal-to-entropy boundary.  At the Lipschitz endpoint \(s=1\), an explicit four-fold scan--refine--invert sample map attains the known-cutoff order once \(T_n=n\kappa_n^3\) dominates \(\log(e/\kappa_n)\).  For \(s>1\), the prescribed kernel argmax is not uniformly centered under the stated observable-smoothness class because an unrestricted cross-cutoff slope kink can dominate the shrinking level jump; the critical-window frontier and a strong-signal construction robust to that nuisance remain unresolved.

project_justification.gap: Weak fuzzy-RD inference is honest at a known cutoff, and unknown-cutoff theory localizes directly observed fixed or shrinking jumps, but neither literature characterizes connected LATE-interval length when the first-stage denominator and its location become weak jointly.
project_justification.niche: The joint experiment has a nonconvex location union, a causal outcome--treatment coupling, and a fixed-level decision loss; its critical window cannot be read from a point-estimation cutoff rate or a known-cutoff weak-instrument inversion.
project_justification.fill: The project defines one observable reduced-form minimax class, embeds outcome-invariant latent monotone location mixtures in it, derives the finite-sample connected-length converse, and supplies a fully specified four-fold bias-aware scan--invert interval with proved oracle-order attainment at \(s=1\).  The proof also isolates an explicit in-class slope-kink obstruction to extending that particular scan to \(s>1\), thereby identifying the additional nuisance geometry that the all-smoothness critical and strong-signal constructions must handle.

body.related_work: Noack and Rothe (2024) motivate the observable class: fuzzy-RD LATE is a ratio of one-sided reduced-form jumps, weak compliance defeats ordinary Wald inference, and bias-aware Anderson--Rubin inversion restores known-cutoff honesty under smooth observed regressions.  Porter and Yu (2015), Theorem 5, prove fixed-jump oracle substitution for treatment-effect estimation after an unknown cutoff in their sharp-design model.  Frick, Munk, and Sieling (2014) motivate the multiscale scan architecture, and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014) provide general maximal-control tools; neither source supplies this uniform localization-to-connected-length theorem.  M{\"u}ller and Song (1997) and Tuvaandorj (2020) analyze vanishing-jump or nonparametric location experiments rather than the causal connected-length target.  Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018) supply the ordered-modulus and test-inversion template on convex fixed-index classes.  Madrid Padilla, Yu, Wang, and Rinaldo (2022) study aligned multivariate change channels without the monotone fuzzy-RD causal constraints.  Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version) use a Bayesian unknown-cutoff fuzzy-RD specification rather than a frequentist honest minimax frontier.  Arai, Otsu, and Seo (2026) discuss fuzzy and unknown-discontinuity extensions separately.  The proved contribution here is the explicit Lipschitz-endpoint scan--refine--invert theorem.  For \(s>1\), the frozen class permits a cross-cutoff derivative kink large enough to displace the prescribed kernel-contrast maximizer, so neither fixed-jump oracle substitution nor known-cutoff Anderson--Rubin inversion closes that case.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The strong-signal theorem is proved only at \(s=1\).  For every \(s>1\), a legal linear-slope witness makes the specified \(K_1\) population contrast peak away from the true cutoff because \(H/\kappa_n\to\infty\).  No larger sample-size constant repairs that population bias.  A full \(s>1\) upper bound must use a slope-robust cutoff criterion under the same class, not import latent-cell smoothness or cross-side derivative compatibility.  The sharp fixed-\(\alpha\) critical-window law remains open for every \(s\).
body.honest_scope: The Wald interpretation, location-mixture barriers, and known-cutoff benchmark retain their stated scope over the full class.  The explicit strong-signal oracle-attainment result is uniform over the Lipschitz face \(s=1\), allows \(\kappa_n\to0\), and concerns honest connected expected length.  It is not asserted for \(s>1\): the class controls the two one-sided observable extensions separately but does not control their derivative mismatch.  No cross-side derivative condition, latent-cell H\"older condition, covariance eigenvalue floor, adaptation claim, disconnected-set claim, or Bayesian calibration claim is added.  The all-\(s\) critical-window expression and an attaining interval remain the paper's open frontier question.
body.interpretation: At \(s=1\), localization information \(n\kappa_n^3\) pays once for the unknown cutoff; after localization, independent fixed-center inversion has the same \(n^{-1/3}/\kappa_n\) length as if the cutoff were supplied.  The higher-smoothness obstruction is deterministic rather than a missing concentration constant: separate smooth extensions on the two sides do not control their derivative mismatch, and that mismatch can move the scan's population peak by order \(H\).
